## Natural history notes

A small mason bee characterized by its dark metallic blue-green to bluish-black body, sturdy build, and habit of carrying pollen on the underside of the abdomen rather than on the hind legs. In Florida, it is found in gardens, forest edges, parks, pine flatwoods, roadsides, and other habitats with flowering plants and suitable nesting cavities. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while females nest in hollow stems, beetle burrows, or other small cavities, using mud or plant material to partition brood cells for their young.
